items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: He was in the world, played sax with him a long time out there.

ctx.x: I just wondered, didn't they have some other bands that came over here that you'd hear and maybe sit in with? Yes.

Sam Morgan was here, he was the drawing card here. Rainey, Punch Miller, Buddy PT. I can't think of his name right now, but they had a lot of bands come out of here. But the man that gave me my inspiration was Joe Watson. He was playing Craneet with Sam Morgan. He was a very sweet Craneet player. And I used to stay right under him every time he'd come here. I was right under him. I liked the way he played Craneet. Chris Kelly, he was out of here. Used to come out here a lot. Who did he have with him? I'm sorry.
Go ahead. I was just playing for Sam, of course. Who did he have with him, Chris, when he was here, Your Honor? Who was brought to him?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-15
items.q: I liked it, uh, Joe Watson with Sam Morgan.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you, who were some of the best clarinet players in New Orleans when you first came here?
Oh, when I first came here, I liked it, uh, Joe Watson with Sam Morgan.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: If you play with Sam Morgan you might see his pictures of his band.

ctx.x: Oh, wow. I just wanted to get him straight. Yeah. So I'd know who he was.

Uh-huh. Then I played with Rene and he'd come over there. As a matter of fact, I played with Rene here. But he first known me from over there. Uh, when Jim Robson used to come over there with Sam Morgan, I was a little boy then. And he used to come over there with Sam Morgan when I used to play with him. And then Isaiah Morgan made up him a band. He used to come over there. He used to play with him. I played with Isaiah a long time. And then Tom Albert come to play with my daddy. Well, he told me I was a heard me…
What kind of cornet did he play? Did he play straight or hard?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: I mentioned the few I heard. As a matter of fact, I heard practically all of them... Such as Sam Morgan...

ctx.x: Well, it's his daddy then. That's what I wanted to get straight.

Yeah, his daddy. Uh-huh. Uh. Well, after I left, uh, Pelican, I left here and went to St. Louis. Worked at the Democratic Club there. Uh-huh. Under a fellow by the name of Hawkins. At the Democratic Club at that time. My Bobby Gordon up there, it was through our, uh, Charlie Chris. Used to work with, with Faith Morgan. He played trumpet and he played, uh, the accordion. Oh. He's dead now, a fellow. Uh, up there I had, uh, I can't remember this guy's name. I don't remember one man's name up there. Was playing with…
